findings.title: Storage create failure recorded as a legacy duration
findings.body: When Storage.Create fails, the code calls recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration. The failure is attributed to the wrong backend, so legacy error metrics are inflated and storage error metrics are missed. The same bug is in Update (line 129).

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection duration recorded as storage metric
findings.body: The async legacy DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration with the legacy start time and the legacy error. This pollutes the storage metrics and leaves the legacy metrics without data for this operation. It should call recordLegacyDuration.

findings.title: Delete context uses d.Log instead of the enriched log
findings.body: ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) discards the log that was built with name, kind and method values. Downstream logging therefore loses that context. It should pass `log`.

findings.title: Delete success metric labelled with name instead of kind
findings.body: On success, recordStorageDuration is called with `name` where every other call passes options.Kind. This produces a high-cardinality, inconsistent metric label.

findings.title: Async legacy write reuses request context
findings.body: The goroutines derive their context from the request ctx. When the HTTP request finishes and its context is cancelled, the legacy write is cancelled with it, so legacy writes may silently never happen. Use context.WithoutCancel(ctx), or a background context that keeps the values, as the base. The Update, Delete and DeleteCollection goroutines have the same problem.

findings.title: Legacy Update reuses objInfo after Storage update
findings.body: The async legacy Update is passed the original objInfo and runs concurrently with, and after, the request. It computes the update from legacy state rather than from the object Storage just wrote. The old code wrapped the result in updateWrapper to keep the two consistent. Legacy can now diverge, for example on PATCH or when the update is computed from stale data. Errors from the async legacy write are also not logged.
